 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix is bringing a plethora of off-track festivities alongside racing action. Away from the high-speed adrenaline, fans will also get to see Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc up close, thanks to a joint appearance at Puma's flagship store in the city. Titled 'Under the Lights,' the special event is scheduled for Tuesday, November 17, from 6 PM to 8 PM local time, bringing Ferrari's two drivers together for an evening celebrating motorsport, fashion and entertainment.
 With the Vegas Strip gearing up for another high-profile evening, the event will be hosted by Mexican singer and television personality Paty Cantú, while the internationally recognized Jabbawockeez dance crew will provide additional entertainment. A live DJ will also be part of the program, suggesting that Puma is looking to create more of a lifestyle experience than a conventional driver appearance.
 Both Hamilton and Leclerc are prominent faces of Puma's partnership with Scuderia Ferrari HP, meaning the upcoming appeal is also part of the marketing duties that come under the drivers' contracts.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Puma has increasingly used Formula 1 race weekends to connect its performance sportswear identity with streetwear, fashion and popular culture. Notably, the event does not require any separate ticket purchases or admission fees, but with limited seats available, it is on a first-come, first-served basis.
 While there is no confirmation of whether the appearance will include autograph or photograph opportunities, the chance to see Hamilton and Leclerc together away from the paddock remains a major draw.
 Not the First Time Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton Are Doing a Puma Event in Vegas
 The upcoming event isn't the first time Hamilton and Leclerc will be partnering up to bring some Ferrari star power to a Puma event in Las Vegas. The duo was also at the sports-lifestyle brand's flagship store last year and engaged with the fans as well.
 Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton also attended Puma's fan event in 2025. (Source: MEGA)
 The event attracted considerable attention from Ferrari supporters, who turned up hoping to catch a glimpse of the Scuderia teammates away from the paddock. It also underlined how PUMA has been using Formula 1's Las Vegas stop to create experiences that extend beyond the racing weekend.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Moreover, Puma's Vegas activation has almost become a tradition now, given the brand also held a session in 2024. Since Hamilton wasn't a part of the band at the time, Leclerc was joined by then-teammate Carlos Sainz for the session, as they celebrated the launch of the Puma x Ferrari Desert Sun collection.
 At the time, the event marked the opening of Puma's flagship store in Vegas and featured merchandise customization, sim-racing activities, and an exclusive meet-and-greet with 20 selected fans, who received photographs and autographs with the drivers. The first 100 customers purchasing from the collection also received limited-edition Las Vegas tote bags.
 Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc Also Have Personal Launches Coming Up
 With the arrival of the Las Vegas GP, Puma and Ferrari have already announced a special event involving both Ferrari drivers. There are chances that a new line of items will also be launched for fans to get hold of, particularly given the fact that the team will be donning a special black and gold suit for the entire weekend.
 Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc have their own brand events lined up in Vegas. (Source: MEGA)
 But while all that goes on, each driver will also be busy on the personal end, given that both their fashion brands are launching new lineups as well. While Leclerc's CL16 brand has already gone live with its Fall 2026 collection , the Monegasque driver will be taking the opportunity to promote his newest releases.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Meanwhile, Hamilton is also coming to Vegas, keeping his own tradition alive by setting up a Plus44 pop-up . The British driver's past pop-ups have been all about creativity and expression with different themes and collabs, and this year is no different. While most of the details remain under wraps, the Briton has revealed that this year's merch will be an alien-themed release.
